verifiedEndpoints.codePaths: provisioner uses incluster_client (Kubernetes API), PostgresStore (gateway-db), DNS; refresh_registry only reconfigures the registry and does not contact MCP servers

sourceChanges.helm/urumi/values.yaml: storeProvisioner.apiServerEgress: [] (opt-in; empty keeps the older rule)
sourceChanges.helm/urumi/templates/networkpolicy.yaml: store-provisioner-net: one rule per apiServerEgress entry (ipBlock cidr, TCP port); the older 443/6443 rule with no destination renders only when the list is empty
sourceChanges.helm/urumi/templates/_helpers.tpl: validate each entry: map with cidr and port, cidr /32 or /128, not 0.0.0.0, port 1-65535

tests: helm template values-disposable.yaml and values-disposable-proposed.yaml (with probe CIDRs) -> render ok

candidateRender.diffVsRev8: urumi-store-provisioner-net only: the destination-free 443/6443 rule is replaced by 10.96.0.1/32:443 and 172.19.0.2/32:6443

uncertainties: With iptables kube-proxy, Calico sees the post-DNAT destination, so 172.19.0.2:6443 is the rule that matches today; 10.96.0.1:443 is kept for a dataplane that evaluates before DNAT and is not proven needed here
If the Kind node IP changes, the provisioner loses API access until the value is updated; failure is closed (provisioning stalls), not open
Tracked defaults keep the older destination-free rule when the list is empty, so other installs stay as before until they set the value
The pod is not restarted by this change; established connections may persist until they reconnect
